1.why: All seven screens are static cards with no animation, carousels or pop-up dialogs; only the dark Logs panel adds visual noise, otherwise the layout is clean and uncluttered.

2.why: Bold headings, a highlighted step chip, a status banner and a single filled teal primary button make the key element on each screen stand out, though the large black Logs box competes for attention.

3.why: The single input and primary button are easy to spot, but the required recovery code is buried in a dark developer 'Logs' panel as a 64-character hex string, which makes finding what she needs slow and confusing.

4.why: The persistent 1–5 step bar, per-step instructions and 'no session countdown' note reduce memory load, but she must still transcribe a long code and recall the 12-character/uppercase/number/symbol password rules while typing.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, no show-password toggle, no autofill/password-manager hint or suggestion appears on any screen, including the sign-in step.

6.why: Nothing saved or familiar is surfaced — no pre-filled or masked email, no remembered account, no saved device recognition — only the layout itself is repeated.

7.why: Every screen uses short, plain sentences in large readable type, e.g. 'Password saved. Sign in when you are ready.' with no dense blocks of text.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the seven screenshots, so the claim cannot be confirmed; only success/status banners are visible.

9.why: Password rules are stated in words but no example password, no email placeholder and no worked example of the code entry are provided; the only guidance is 'The simulated code is in the Logs panel.'

10.why: The available options are clearly labelled ('Recovery code', 'New password', 'Verification code', 'Sign in'), though only password/code methods exist with no biometric alternative.

11.why: Each screen presents one primary action (at most two buttons on the verify step), so she is never faced with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Each action produces an explicit outcome banner — 'Code verified', 'Password saved', 'Identity confirmed. You are signed in', 'Privacy statement accepted' — plus a log entry.

13.why: A 'Need help?' link is present on every step and each screen carries a short guiding tip such as 'Start when you are ready. We will guide you one step at a time.'

14.why: Step 2 offers 'Send a new recovery code' with an explanation, but there is no back button, edit-email option or visible retry path on the other steps.

15.why: All seven screens reuse the same header, step chips, banner, form and button styling in the same positions, so the pattern is highly learnable.
